simulation.organization_and_actor: medium or large Brazilian hospital or SUS hospital network; hospital operations manager and pharmacy supply coordinator
processes: forecast bed and emergency demand and allocate constrained capacity
forecast medication consumption and recommend reorder or redeployment quantities
plan staffing and operating-room capacity under demand uncertainty
deterministic_and_statistical_baselines: minimum/maximum stock, reorder point, safety stock and expiry rules
moving averages, seasonal forecasting and constrained mathematical optimization

technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: stock movements, substitutions, shortages, delayed postings and exceptional clinical demand can make observed consumption differ from unconstrained need; random splits would leak seasonality and policy changes

training_data.observation_unit: medication-SKU by hospital unit and day, or capacity unit by time interval
training_data.input_data: historical dispensing or consumption, current stock, expiry, purchase lead time, scheduled procedures, admissions, occupancy, seasonality and operational constraints
training_data.target_or_reward: future demand and downstream service-level, expiry, shortage and inventory-cost outcomes
training_data.label_source: later stock movements, dispensations, admissions, occupancy and validated shortage or expiry events
training_data.prediction_time: before purchasing, transfer, staffing or capacity-allocation decisions
training_data.expected_volume: unknown; must be measured per hospital, SKU and unit
training_data.class_balance: intermittent demand and rare shortage events likely; unknown until profiling
training_data.historical_coverage: daily BNAFAR reporting improves availability in SUS, but local completeness, substitutions and hospital-unit granularity remain unknown
training_data.train_validation_split: rolling or forward-chaining split by time, with holdout periods covering seasonal and policy changes
training_data.leakage_risks: post-decision stock corrections, emergency purchases, later substitutions, discharge information and future procedure changes
training_data.representativeness_risks: hospital case mix, formulary, procurement cycles and local reporting quality vary materially
training_data.feedback_loop: pharmacist and operations overrides plus realized demand, shortage, waste and service-level outcomes
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: prefer aggregated operational data; patient-level linkage only when necessary and governed under LGPD and clinical access controls
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use deterministic inventory policy, statistical seasonal baseline and scenario-based optimization without learned forecasts

portfolio_coherence.material_differentiation: none sufficient: hospital capacity forecasting overlaps HEALTH-001, while pharmacy inventory forecasting and optimization is a mature product category and largely an adoption/integration problem

existing_landscape.notes: BNAFAR already provides daily stock and movement reporting infrastructure; commercial hospital-pharmacy platforms already forecast demand, recommend PAR/reorder levels and prioritize expiry redeployment. A separate repository opportunity would duplicate established capabilities without a specific uncovered operational boundary.
